title: Cap. III Rat. 14: conformity of decree and temporal execution — Achilles of foresight-election
pass_a_gloss: Reason 14. Last in place they argue from the conformity which is between the decree of the Divine election itself and the temporal execution of the same, in this manner: In the same order in which things in time are put into execution, God from eternity decreed that they should be put. For it belongs to the immutability of the Divine will, that he not act otherwise in time than from all eternity he decreed that he would act. Since therefore in the temporal execution of the elect's salvation he leads no one to glory except in view of good works and final perseverance, he could not from eternity otherwise elect them to glory except from the same view. For if before the foundations of the world were laid he elected them to glory gratuitously, and not from foreseen works, and when it comes to execution he is unwilling to give them glory except from works, he has changed his will, which is most unworthy of the Divine wisdom. All the Papists who contend that election is made from foreseen works trust greatly in this argument, and boast that it is as it were Achilles.
pass_b_english: Rat. 14. Last they argue from the conformity between God's election decree and its temporal execution: in the same order in which things are executed in time, God from eternity decreed they should be executed. Divine immutability requires he not act otherwise in time than he from eternity decreed he would. So since in temporal execution he leads none of the elect to glory except in view of good works and final perseverance, he could not from eternity elect them to glory except under that same view. If before the world's foundations he elected them to glory freely, not from foreseen works, yet at execution will not give glory except from works, he has changed his will — most unworthy of divine wisdom. All Papists who hold election from foreseen works trust this argument heavily and boast it is their Achilles.
source_text: Rat. 14. Ultimo in loco argumentantur a conformitate quae est inter ipsum decretum electionis Divinae et temporalem exsecutionem ejusdem, hanc in modum; Eodem ordine quo res in tempore mandantur exsecutioni, Deus ab aeternitate decrevit ut mandarentur. Pertinet enim ad immutabilitatem voluntatis Divinae, ut non aliter agat in tempore, quam ab omni aeternitate se acturum esse decrevit. Quandoquidem igitur in temporali exsecutione salutis electorum, neminem perducit ad gloriam nisi intuitu bonorum operum et perseverantiae finalis, non potuit ab aeterno aliter ad gloriam illos eligere nisi ex eodem intuitu. Nam si ante jacta mundi fundamenta illos ad gloriam elegit gratuito, et non ex operibus praevisis, et cum ad exsecutionem ventum fuerit, non vult illis dare gloriam nisi ex operibus, mutavit voluntatem suam, quod est Divina sapientia indignissimum. Omnes Papistae qui electionem ex operibus praevisis fieri contendunt, huic argumento valde confidunt, et quasi Achilleum esse jactitant.
